Global Growth and Economic Cycle
Aggregates commodity positioning, cycle momentum proxies, and metals-led demand signals to assess the current global growth and economic cycle regime.

Regime Assessment:

  • Regime: Transitional / Fragile Balance.
  • Regime Confidence Index: Medium Confidence.
  • Status: The regime is fragile.

Why This Regime:

  • High-weight industrial signals confirm expansionary demand and sponsorship builds (1)(2).
  • Dynamic weighting prioritizes structural tailwinds and high-conviction copper flows over mixed tactical data (1)(2).
  • Fading speculative sponsorship in gold indicates haven exhaustion (3).
  • Crude oil (4) and platinum (5) are downweighted due to low interpretation confidence and internal conflict.

Alignment & Tensions:

  • Copper and silver reinforce an expansionary trend with positive flow sponsorship (1)(6).
  • Lithium (7) and palladium (8) align on bullish reversal risks from extreme levels.
  • Bearish divergence in gold creates tension between price action and capital sponsorship (3).
  • Structural industrial strength offsets tactical haven de-risking, maintaining the transitional balance (2).

Scenario Balance:

  • Dominant scenario: Idiosyncratic industrial demand expansion while energy and currency headwinds remain secondary.
  • Primary upside risk: A short squeeze in battery metals triggered by speculative exhaustion (7).
  • Primary downside risk: Broad long liquidation if rates flow momentum fails to sustain its recovery (9).

What Would Change the Regime:

  • Copper speculative Z-score exceeding +2.0, signaling structural long crowding (1).
  • Metals Tailwind robust z-score falling below +0.75, invalidating the idiosyncratic demand narrative (2).
  • A rise in contrarian flow shares within the rates sector (9).
